今日[きょう]の お勧[すす]めは？

Travel

今日の (きょうの, kyō no) means "today's," and the question word は (wa) marks the topic of the sentence, which is "today's recommendation." · You'll notice that this isn't a compelte sentence. The complete version of this sentence would be 今日のお勧めは何ですか？In Japanese it is very common to trail off and let the person you are talking to finish your sentnece with a response. It's strange for English speakers at first, but you'll get used to it over time.

This phrase is a polite request to ask for something to be made less sweet.
